title: Ethics and virtue ethics
competency: Explain virtue ethics, tell virtues from vices and use the steps of ethical decision making.

keywords.def: Ethics that judges right and wrong by what a person of good character (a "virtuous agent") would do.
A good character trait, like honesty, compassion or courage.
A bad habit, the opposite of a virtue, like dishonesty, cowardice or selfishness.
The study of what is good or bad, right or wrong, in daily life.

en.text: Virtue ethics is about building good character so we become good citizens. Virtues are good habits like honesty, courage and generosity; vices are their opposites, like dishonesty, cowardice and selfishness. Virtue is not inborn: we learn it by practice and by imitating good people.

screens.title: The fox in the well
screens.ask: A fox falls into a well. A wolf says, "Poor fellow, I pity you!" but walks on without helping. Was that kind?
opts: No: kind words without action are not enough
Yes, he said he pitied him
Yes, it was not his problem
The fox was wrong to fall
screens.after: Real virtue shows in action. The fox said: "Get me out, and I'll know you're sorry."

screens.title: Virtue ethics
paras: Virtue ethics is about developing one's character to prepare for good citizenship.
A community of people with good character is a good community.
Virtues are habits or characteristics that help a community function well.
Virtue is acquired through practice and by imitating virtuous people.

screens.title: Virtues and vices
paras: A virtue is a character trait that makes a person good.
A vice is a bad habit, the opposite of a virtue.

opts: Not yet: a virtuous person has all virtues and no vices

en.text: Ethics studies what is good or bad, right or wrong in daily life. Virtue ethics, mainly from Aristotle, judges an action by a person's character. To solve an ethical problem, follow five steps: identify the problem, identify stakeholders, find solutions, evaluate them, then choose and justify the best.

screens.title: A hard choice
screens.ask: Your friend asks to copy your exam answers. What should you do first to decide well?
opts: Understand the problem and who it affects
screens.after: Good decisions start by understanding the problem and who will be affected. That is the first of five steps.

screens.title: Ethics
paras: Ethics is the study of what good and bad ends to pursue, and what is right and wrong to do.
It sets reasonable standards for making ethical decisions.
Virtue ethics, developed mainly by Aristotle, stresses a person's character rather than rules or consequences.

screens.title: Steps in ethical decision making
items: Research and study until the whole problem is understood.
Who will be affected by the decision?
Develop all the possible courses of action.
Weigh strengths and weaknesses of each option.
Choose the best option and explain why.
